facts.statement: Haast's eagle is classified as the species Hieraaetus moorei.
facts.quote:
genus: Hieraaetus
species: moorei

facts.statement: Julius von Haast first scientifically described Haast's eagle in 1871.
facts.quote: Haast's eagle was first scientifically described by Julius von Haast in 1871

facts.statement: The remains used to describe Haast's eagle were discovered by Frederick Richardson Fuller in a former marsh.
facts.quote: from remains discovered by the Canterbury Museum taxidermist, Frederick Richardson Fuller, in a former marsh

facts.statement: Haast's eagle lived during the Pleistocene to the Late Holocene.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Pleistocene to Late Holocene

facts.statement: Haast's eagle became extinct around 1445.
facts.quote: Haast's eagle became extinct around 1445

facts.statement: Haast's eagle is estimated to have diverged from smaller eagles between 700,000 and 1.8 million years ago.
facts.quote: H. moorei is estimated to have diverged from these smaller eagles as recently as 1.8 million to 700,000 years ago

facts.statement: Recent taxonomists have placed Haast's eagle in the genus Aquila.
facts.quote: It was placed in the genus Aquila by recent taxonomists

facts.statement: Haast's eagle had a relatively short wingspan, estimated at up to 2.6 meters for females, possibly reaching 3 meters in some cases.
facts.quote: It had a relatively short wingspan for its size. It is estimated that the grown female typically spanned up to 2.6 m, possibly up to 3 m in a few cases

facts.statement: Haast's eagle talons were similar to the harpy eagle, with front-left talons measuring 4.9 to 6.15 cm and a hallux-claw possibly up to 11 cm.
facts.quote: The talons of Haast's eagle were similar in length to those of the harpy eagle, with a front-left talon length of 4.9 to 6.15 cm and a hallux-claw of possibly up to 11 cm

facts.statement: Biologist Richard Holdaway proposed in 2025 that 'Fuller's eagle' is a more suitable name than 'Haast's eagle' after reflecting on the naming history.
facts.quote: In an article in 2025, the biologist Richard Holdaway said he had coined the now-conventional common name Haast's eagle in the early 1990s but on later reflection proposes a more suitable name be Fuller's eagle, after its actual discoverer

facts.statement: Haast's eagles acted as top predators in New Zealand, filling the ecological niche of large mammalian hunters.
facts.quote: Haast's eagles were the hunters who filled the same niche as top-niche mammalian predators.

facts.statement: Haast's eagles were specialized hunters dependent on native medium and large-sized flightless birds, unlike adaptable humans.
facts.quote: Unlike the adaptable humans, eagles were dependent on the native medium and large-sized flightless birds, being specialised in hunting them.

facts.statement: Haast's eagles likely competed with Māori for food, and the eagle population went extinct around the same time as its prey, the moa, which died out between 1440 and 1445.
facts.quote: The added hunting pressure from the Māori led the moa to extinction by around 1440 to 1445. Both eagles and Māori likely competed for the same foods.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Māori legends referring to 'hakawai' and 'hōkioi' describe Haast's eagle or the extinct South Island Austral snipe.
facts.quote: However, it has also been argued that the "hakawai" and "hōkioi" legends refer to the Austral snipe—in particular the extinct South Island species.

facts.statement: Some researchers suggest the Māori legend 'pouākai' does not refer to Haast's eagle because the species is not known to have lived on the North Island.
facts.quote: Additionally, it has been suggested that the pouākai is unlikely to refer to Haast's eagle as the species is not known to have been present at North Island.

facts.statement: The species was originally described by Julius von Haast in 1872.
facts.quote: species_authority: (Haast, 1872)

facts.statement: The species was previously known by the synonyms Harpagornis moorei and Harpagomis assimilis.
facts.quote: synonyms: Harpagornis moorei Haast, 1872 Harpagomis assimilis Haast, 1874

facts.statement: Haast's eagle is the largest eagle known to science.
facts.quote: Fue el águila de mayor tamaño que se conoce.

facts.statement: The eagle's main prey were moas, giant flightless birds that could not defend themselves against the eagle's impact force and speed, which could reach 80 km/h.
facts.quote: Su presa principal eran moas, aves gigantes no voladoras e incapaces de defenderse de la fuerza de choque y la velocidad de estas águilas, las cuales podían alcanzar una velocidad de 80 km/h.

facts.statement: The eagle's large size may have been an evolutionary response to prey size, growing substantially over time due to a lack of competition, a process known as insular gigantism.
facts.quote: El gran tamaño del águila puede haber sido una respuesta evolutiva al tamaño de sus presas, ya que habría sido sustancialmente menor cuando arribó a la isla, para luego crecer sustancialmente a lo largo del tiempo debido a la carencia de competencia (véase gigantismo insular).

facts.statement: The eagle was originally described by Julius von Haast in the 1870s based on remains discovered by taxidermist Frederick Richardson Fuller in an old swamp.
facts.quote: El águila de Haast fue descrita originalmente por Julius von Haast en la década de 1870, a partir de restos descubiertos por el taxidermista del Museo Canterbury, Frederick Richardson Fuller, en un antiguo pantano.

facts.statement: The genus name is derived from the Greek words 'harpax' meaning 'snatch' and 'ornis' meaning 'bird'.
facts.quote: El nombre del género se deriva del griego "harpax", que significa 'arpeo', y "ornis", que significa 'ave'.

facts.statement: The species may have diverged from its relatives in a relatively recent period between 700,000 and 1.8 million years ago.
facts.quote: H. moorei puede haber divergido de estas aguilillas en un período relativamente reciente, comprendido entre 700 000 a 1.8 millones de años.

facts.statement: A later mitochondrial DNA study determined the species was more closely related to the Australian goshawk than the booted eagle, with an estimated divergence of 2.2 million years from the goshawk.
facts.quote: Un estudio posterior de ADN mitocondrial determinó que se relacionaba más cercanamente con la aguililla australiana que con la aguililla calzada, con una divergencia evolutiva de la aguililla australiana estimada en cerca de 2.2 millones de años.

facts.statement: Harpagornis was the largest known raptor, slightly larger than the largest vultures and similar in size to the extinct species Amplibuteo woodwardi.
facts.quote: Las águilas de Haast fueron las mayores rapaces conocidas, levemente mayores incluso que los más grandes buitres y con un tamaño parecido al de la especie extinta Amplibuteo woodwardi.

facts.statement: Estimates place female Harpagornis weight between 10 and 15 kg and male weight around 9 to 12 kg.
facts.quote: Muchas estimaciones sitúan a las águilas de Haast hembras en el rango de 10 a 15 kg y a los machos en alrededor de 9 a 12 kg.

facts.statement: One source estimated that the largest females could have weighed more than 16.5 kg.
facts.quote: Una fuente estimó que las mayores hembras pudieron haber llegado a pesar más de 16.5 kg de masa.

facts.statement: Harpagornis had a relatively short wingspan for its size, measuring approximately 2.6 to over 3 meters in some cases.
facts.quote: Tenían una envergadura relativamente corta para su tamaño, midiendo aproximadamente 2.6 hasta más de 3 m en algunos casos.

facts.statement: The lower mandible of Harpagornis measured 11.4 cm in length, and the tarsus measured between 22.7 and 24.9 cm in various fossils.
facts.quote: Una mandíbula inferior del águila de Haast medía 11,4 centímetros de largo y el tarso en varios fósiles ha sido medido entre 22,7 a 24,9 centímetros.

facts.statement: Harpagornis talons were similar in length to those of the harpy eagle, with a front-left claw measuring 4.9 to 6.15 cm and a hallux claw possibly over 11 cm.
facts.quote: Las garras del águila de Haast eran similares en longitud a las del águila harpía, con una longitud frontal-izquierda de 4,9 a 6,15 centímetros y una garra del hallux de posiblemente más de 11 centímetros.

facts.statement: The tail was certainly very long, over 50 cm in female specimens, and very wide.
facts.quote: La cola era seguramente muy larga, de más de 50 centímetros en los especímenes hembra, y muy ancha.

facts.statement: The total body length is estimated at over 1.4 meters in females, with a standing height of approximately 90 cm or slightly more.
facts.quote: Se estima la longitud corporal total en más de 1,4 metros en la hembras, con una altura en posición erguida de aproximadamente 90 centímetros o quizás levemente mayor.

facts.statement: Harpagornis preyed on large flightless birds including moas, which could weigh more than fifteen times the weight of the raptor.
facts.quote: Las águilas de Haast depredaban a las grandes especies de aves no voladoras, incluyendo a las moas, las cuales llegaban a sobrepesar por más de quince veces el peso de la rapaz.

facts.statement: It is estimated that Harpagornis attacked at speeds of over 80 km/h, often gripping the prey's pelvis with one foot and killing it with a blow to the head or neck with the other.
facts.quote: Se estima que atacaba a velocidades de más de 80 kilómetros por hora, con frecuencia aferrándose a la pelvis de la presa con las garras de un pie y matándola con un golpe a la cabeza o el cuello con el otro pie.

facts.statement: Its size and weight indicate that it exerted a striking force equivalent to a block of cement falling from an eight-story building.
facts.quote: Su tamaño y peso indican que ejercía una fuerza corporal de golpe equivalente al de un bloque de cemento que cae desde lo alto de un edificio de ocho pisos.

facts.statement: Its large beak may have been used to tear the internal organs of its prey, causing death by blood loss.
facts.quote: Su gran pico también pudo haber sido usado para rasgar los órganos internos de su presa, causándole la muerte por pérdida de sangre.

facts.statement: Harpagornis lived from the Late Pleistocene to the Holocene, between 0.129 and 0 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Late Pleistocene to Holocene (0.129 to 0 million years ago)

facts.statement: Harpagornis belongs to the parent group Accipitridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Accipitridae

facts.statement: Harpagornis is classified in the family Accipitridae.
facts.quote: Family: Accipitridae

facts.statement: It is debated whether Maori legends about "Hakawai" and "Hokioi" actually refer to the extinct South Island sub-species of the genus Coenocorypha rather than Harpagornis.
facts.quote: No obstante, se ha planteado que las leyendas sobre el "Hakawai" y el "Hokioi" se refieren en realidad a la chochita del género Coenocorypha —en particular a la extinta subespecie de la Isla Sur—.
